title: Quick Weeknight Lasagne
subtitle: Layered pasta with jarred tomato sauce and a two-minute white sauce
excerpt: Quick weeknight lasagne cuts the usual two-hour build to about 45 minutes by using a good jarred tomato sauce and a simple white sauce made in five minutes. The result is  good rather than a compromise, and on a weeknight the difference in effort between this and ordering in is the point.
sourceNotes: A simplified weeknight approach to lasagne al forno that trades authenticity for speed without losing the structure of the dish. The white sauce method is a standard quick roux.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze before baking. Thaw overnight and bake from cold at 190°C covered for 40 minutes, uncovered for 15 more.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Assemble up to 24 hours ahead and refrigerate. Add 15 minutes covered to the bake time.

content.text: Quick weeknight lasagne uses beef mince browned with onion and garlic, then combined with a good jarred tomato sauce to skip the 90-minute simmer. A simple white sauce made from butter, flour, and milk takes five minutes. The layering takes another ten. The oven does the rest. It is not the same dish as a slow-cooked bolognese lasagne, but it is a proper layered pasta bake rather than a shortcut that produces something dry and disappointing.

Heat the oven to 190°C (fan 170°C / gas mark 5). Heat {{olive-oil}} of oil in a wide frying pan over a high heat. Add {{onion}} of onion and cook for 5 minutes until softened. Add {{beef-mince}} of mince and break it up with a spoon. Cook over high heat for 5 to 6 minutes until the meat is brown and any liquid has evaporated. Add {{garlic}} of garlic, {{tomato-puree}} of tomato puree, and {{oregano-dried}} of dried oregano and cook for 1 minute. Add {{tinned-tomatoes}} of tinned tomatoes and {{salt-table}} of salt. Simmer for 10 minutes.
Make the white sauce and assemble

Melt {{unsalted-butter}} of butter in a saucepan. Add {{plain-flour}} of flour and stir for 2 minutes. Whisk in {{whole-milk}} of warm milk gradually and cook over medium heat, stirring, for 4 to 5 minutes until thick. Season with {{nutmeg}} of nutmeg and a pinch of salt.

Spread a thin layer of white sauce on the base of a baking dish. Add {{lasagne-sheets}} of lasagne sheets in a layer. Spread half the meat sauce, then a layer of white sauce. Repeat: pasta, remaining meat sauce, white sauce. Finish with a final layer of pasta and the remaining white sauce. Scatter {{cheddar}} of grated cheddar over the top.
Cover with foil and bake for 25 minutes. Remove the foil and bake for a further 15 minutes until the cheese is golden and the edges are bubbling. Rest for 10 minutes before cutting.

items.symptom: The pasta sheets are hard in the middle
items.cause: The sauce layers were too thin and did not provide enough moisture for the dried sheets to absorb.
items.fix: Ensure each pasta layer is generously coated with sauce on both sides. If the assembled dish looks dry, pour 100 ml of water around the edges before covering with foil.

items.symptom: The lasagne is swimming in liquid when cut
items.cause: The meat sauce had too much liquid, or the dish was cut before resting.
items.fix: Reduce the meat sauce until it is thick before assembling. Always rest the lasagne for 10 minutes after baking; it firms up as it cools.

content.text: This is the version that most British home cooks make on a Wednesday: the bones of the Italian original reassembled with available ingredients and practical cooking time. The long-cooked ragù and fresh spinach pasta of the Bolognese original become a 20-minute mince sauce and dried no-cook sheets. The trade-off is real but the result is still layered pasta bake rather than something to apologise for. The leftovers are usually better than the first serving.
